title: Fish Pie
subtitle: Creamy fish and prawn pie under a mashed potato crust
excerpt: A British classic with chunks of cod, salmon, and prawns in a rich white sauce, topped with golden mashed potato. It takes a little time to put together but almost everything can be done ahead. It freezes well and reheats from frozen without losing much quality.
sourceNotes: Based on the traditional British fish pie, a comfort food staple found across home kitchens and pub menus throughout the UK.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before the final bake. Defrost in the fridge overnight and bake as directed, adding 10 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Divide between two dishes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 1 day ahead. Cover and refrigerate until ready to bake.

content.text: Poach the fish gently in the milk used for the sauce; this adds flavour without wasting anything. Keep the fish in large chunks so it stays intact once the pie is assembled and baked.
Boil the potato in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender. Drain well, then mash with 30g of the butter and the double cream. Season and set aside.
Pour the milk into a large saucepan. Add the cod and salmon, bring to a very gentle simmer, and poach for 4 minutes. Lift the fish out with a slotted spoon and set aside. Keep the milk.
In the same saucepan, melt the remaining 30g of butter over a medium heat. Add the leek and soften for 5 minutes. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes.
Gradually pour in the warm poaching milk, whisking as you go. Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season and stir in the parsley.
Arrange the poached fish and prawns in a deep baking dish. Pour the sauce over the top.
Spoon the mash over the filling and spread it to the edges. Scatter over the grated parmesan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the topping is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.

items.fix: Reduce the sauce a little more before assembling next time.

items.cause: Filling was too hot when mash was added
items.fix: Let the filling cool slightly before topping with mash.
Poach for only 3 to 4 minutes; it finishes in the oven.
